one_liner: Multithreaded in-memory Rust NoSQL server with a SQL-like query language; one unaudited 2022 benchmark shows ~6x Redis GET/SET throughput.
what_it_does: Skytable is a standalone database server (skyd), not a library. Data lives in RAM in typed 'models' (tables) grouped into 'spaces', and is persisted to custom append-only journals. Clients speak the Skyhash/2 protocol over TCP (TLS optional) and send BlueQL statements (INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/UPSERT/DELETE) with mandatory parameters; every DML statement is a point query on the primary key. It is not Redis-compatible at the wire or command level: 0.8.0 removed the old GET/SET actions, so moving off Redis means defining a schema, using a new client (Rust is stable, Python beta, Node alpha) and rewriting your queries.
how_it_is_fast: In 0.8, each model's primary index is a lock-free concurrent hash trie in the style of Bagwell's hash array mapped trie and Prokopec et al.'s Ctrie (the code also borrows from the contrie crate). It uses 16-way nodes with crossbeam-epoch memory reclamation, and each row sits behind its own parking_lot RwLock, so threads working on different keys do not share a global lock. Networking runs on a tokio multi-threaded runtime with 16 KiB buffered I/O; the release build uses fat LTO, codegen-units=1 and jemalloc. Durability stays off the request path: DML changes go into an in-memory delta that a background service batch-writes to the journal ('delayed durability'). The 2022 benchmark measured the older 0.7.x store (RwLock-sharded hashbrown tables with GET/SET actions), not this engine.
when_to_use: Single-node, multi-core in-memory storage with typed schemas (ints, floats, strings, binary, nested lists) where every read and write is a point lookup or update by primary key.
Write-heavy workloads that can lose the last few minutes of acknowledged writes on a crash in exchange for keeping disk I/O off the request path.
Rust services: the official Apache-2.0 `skytable` crate is the only stable driver and offers sync and async APIs, TLS and connection pooling.
Deployments that need the server to run natively on Windows: x86_64 MSVC is a Tier-1 CI target, and the 2022 poster noted it was the only one of the four stores to run on Windows natively.
Cases where you will benchmark your own workload anyway: the bundled sky-bench tool reports throughput and latency distributions.
when_not_to_use: As a cache: no TTL/expiry, eviction policy or memory cap exists in 0.8 (docs issue #362 asking how to expire keys is unanswered), and the whole dataset must fit in RAM.
As a Redis replacement: it has no RESP protocol, no Redis structures (sorted sets, streams, pub/sub) and no scripting; the 'fully compatible with Redis' request (#271) has been open since 2022.

When writes must be durable: by default DML deltas are flushed every 300 s (rs_window; the example config uses 600), or sooner once a model's pending delta passes about 2% of free memory. A crash can lose minutes of acknowledged writes, and there are no multi-statement DML transactions (#331 is open).
When you need HA, replication or sharding: 0.8.x is single-node only. Clustering (0.9) has been 'nearing completion' since 2025 on the crv1 branch and is unreleased.
When you need range scans, secondary indexes or joins: DML is point queries on the primary key only, and the docs call multi-row ALL operations slow and discouraged.

integration.form: standalone server binary (skyd; prebuilt bundles, .deb, multi-arch Docker images) plus a client crate/driver; not embeddable
integration.dependencies: Server: tokio, tokio-openssl + openssl (vendored, so it is compiled from source), crossbeam-epoch, parking_lot, jemallocator (non-MSVC), serde/serde_yaml, crc, uuid, chrono, rcrypt; windows crate on Windows, libc on Unix. Client: skytable crate (Apache-2.0).
integration.min_toolchain: Server MSRV not documented. CI builds with the latest stable Rust (edition 2021), and the source uses `&raw mut`, which needs Rust 1.82 or newer. Building the vendored OpenSSL needs a C toolchain. The Rust client's MSRV is 1.75.
integration.platforms: Tier-1 in CI: x86_64 Linux, macOS and Windows (MSVC), aarch64 Linux, i686 Linux. aarch64 macOS is 'Tier-1X'. Tier-2: x86_64 musl and 32-bit Windows, and the changelog says 32-bit Windows will likely be deprecated.
integration.thread_safety: Multi-threaded server: at least one worker thread per logical CPU (the docs say this cannot be limited), and a semaphore caps concurrent connections at 50,000. Each single DML statement is applied under a per-row RwLock; there are no multi-statement transactions. The Rust client supports concurrent sync and async use plus pooling.

gotchas: The benchmarked version no longer exists. The June 2022 numbers came from 0.7.x GET/SET actions; 0.8.0 replaced the query API, protocol and in-memory index. The only Skytable-vs-Redis data for 0.8 is a first-party chart from one 6C/12T laptop-class machine, with no numbers in the text.
BlueQL rejects inline string and numeric literals: values must be sent as parameters (the REPL fills them in for you). This breaks hand-written or string-concatenated queries.
A source comment on the 0.8 hash trie warns that its full-size nodes cause 'significant memory blowup' and says the structure will be removed later, so budget RAM generously above your raw data size.

At first start the root password must be at least 16 characters, and the default plaintext endpoint is 127.0.0.1:2003. Development of 0.9 happens partly in a private repo; the maintainer says 0.8 to 0.9 data migration is ready.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: If you need Redis semantics on many cores, pick Valkey, KeyDB or Dragonfly: they speak RESP and support TTL and eviction. Pick Skytable only if you want a schema-based, SQL-like point-query store written in Rust that runs natively on Windows, and you can accept delayed durability and single-node operation. Its speed evidence is weaker than the scripted, versioned runs behind Pogocache.
verified_claims_summary: An anonymous June 2022 HN post ran GET/SET with 30 client threads at 1 connection each between two AWS m5.4xlarge instances and reported Skytable (0.7.x era) at 619,992/676,091 ops/s vs Redis at 112,100/99,892 (about 5.5x GET and 6.8x SET), with KeyDB and Dragonfly in between. It gives no payload size, server versions, build flags or scripts, and does not say which of redis-benchmark, memtier or sky-bench produced each number; Dragonfly's author replied with about 1.02M SET ops/s for Dragonfly on the same instance type at 560 connections, so the result mostly shows multi-threaded servers beating single-threaded Redis at 30 connections.
status_note: Active but in maintenance mode: 0.8.x gets dependency and CLI fixes (a 0.8.5 changelog landed 2026-09-26; the last tagged release is v0.8.4 from 2024-08-07), while clustered 0.9 is still unreleased. It is an AGPL-3.0 server with an Apache-2.0 client and prebuilt binaries, so run it as a service rather than vendoring it.
